premises.text: Existing apps find single venues/events but cannot compose places and events that go together for an occasion
premises.evidence_span: there's not a single product on the market today that can tell you what places and what events go together for your occasion

premises.text: Plans start from mood and companions, optional anchor events, review snippets, and Facebook-personalized itineraries
premises.evidence_span: most people, when planning any social occasion, think of two things. What's my mood and who's coming with me?

premises.text: Algorithmically classifies, ranks, and composes live web places/events into itineraries—never hand-curated
premises.evidence_span: Everything's algorithmically generated. Not a single thing is hand curated

premises.text: Itineraries include review snippets, directions, booking/ticket links, and editable plans friends can advise on via Facebook
premises.evidence_span: You even have relevant information about each place, and you can get directions from place to place to place here, as well as booking links out to OpenTable

premises.text: One-tap Facebook event creation from a WIATA plan for inviting others
premises.evidence_span: What's awesome about making a Facebook event on WIATA is that it's even easier than making a Facebook event on Facebook site itself

value.text: Personal-concierge planning that solves what to do tonight and removes planning hassle
value.evidence_span: It solves the problem of what to do tonight. It also takes all the hassle out of planning it

causal_links.evidence_span: WIATA is a lot like having your own personal concierge
Making plans has never been easier
There's our Facebook event. That happened in less than two seconds

notes: Single-venue gap as problem. Mood/companions/event/Facebook inputs, live algorithmic composition, and review/booking/friend-edit surfaces folded as itinerary product cascade (§4.1.7). Facebook event creation split as distinct social distribution module. Uber tweet promo excluded. Metro expansion as vision framing. Three domains—anti-template.
